# PROJECT LANTERN 4 STATUS REPORT
## Community Library Appointment Pilot

---

## ENTRY 1: 2026-09-08

Project Lantern 4 entered active development phase following vendor selection in August. The pilot targets three municipal library branches in the Westbrook district: Central Library, Riverside Branch, and Hillcrest Commons. Scope encompasses appointment scheduling for patron services including reference consultation (60 min), computer literacy training (90 min), document scanning assistance (45 min), and children's story hour (30 min). The system integrates with existing library staff calendars via middleware adapter. Technical stack: Node.js backend, PostgreSQL database, React frontend, authentication via existing municipal SSO. Database schema initialized with 47 tables covering staff profiles, patron accounts, appointment slots, notification queues, and audit logs. Development team consists of four engineers, one QA specialist, and product lead James Huang. Initial velocity estimate: 12 story points per sprint (two-week cycles). Three critical paths identified: appointment availability display, staff notification subsystem, and cancellation handling workflow. All three paths gate pilot launch. First engineering review scheduled for September 22.

---

## ENTRY 2: 2026-09-22

First sprint completed with 11 of 12 story points delivered. Appointment availability display achieved functional parity with requirements document section 4.2. Frontend renders opening slots for each service type, filtered by branch location and staff assignment. Query performance baseline established: average response time 340ms for full branch availability across 12-week window. Notification subsystem 80% complete; email template system functional, SMS gateway integration pending vendor credential provision (expected by September 29). Cancellation workflow sprint backlog moved to sprint 2 per capacity constraints. QA conducted initial smoke testing of availability display on Chrome, Firefox, and Safari; all major browsers passing. Mobile responsiveness testing on iPhone 14 and Pixel 7 device pool showed no layout issues at standard viewport sizes. Automated test coverage for availability service at 73%. Staff calendar synchronization required retry logic for failed pulls; three-strike timeout with exponential backoff implemented to handle intermittent municipal network outages. Next sprint priorities: SMS notification completion, appointment confirmation flow, and foundational cancellation scaffolding. Risk register updated with vendor credential delay; mitigation path extends SMS launch by one week maximum.

---

## ENTRY 3: 2026-10-06

Sprint 2 progress mixed. Notification subsystem fully deployed and tested end-to-end with municipal SMS provider (Clarity Messaging). Confirmation flow completed: patrons receive email confirmation immediately upon booking, SMS reminder 24 hours before appointment, and post-appointment satisfaction survey link. Confirmation email open rate measured at 64% in staging environment (measured across 287 test messages, October 2-5). SMS delivery rate at 98.3% (one message failed due to invalid phone format in test data). Appointment confirmation feature stories delivered on time. Cancellation workflow, however, encountered scope creep: product team identified seven distinct cancellation scenarios (patron self-service, staff-initiated for emergencies, automatic timeout for no-shows, administrative bulk cancellations, system-generated due to staff unavailability, rescheduling-as-cancellation, and patron request via phone bridge). Initial estimates covered only patron self-service and staff emergency cancellation. Remaining five scenarios require additional database migration and state machine complexity. Cancellation work deferred to sprint 3; this delays critical path by one sprint. Engineering velocity: 11 of 13 points. Database now contains 52 tables. Automated test suite expanded to 184 test cases; code coverage 76%. Mobile testing expanded to include accessibility checks (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance in progress, 82% of checks passing). Staff calendar sync retry logic performing well; zero timeout failures observed across 4,201 synchronization cycles in staging.

---

## ENTRY 4: 2026-10-20

CRITICAL ISSUE IDENTIFIED: During sprint 3 cancellation workflow development, QA uncovered a gap in the no-show timeout path. The scenario: appointment scheduled, patron fails to arrive at scheduled time, system should auto-cancel after 30-minute grace period and free the slot for other patrons. The gap occurs when system attempts to cancel: current state machine does not emit cancellation notifications to freed slots in adjacent appointment windows. Concretely, if a 60-minute appointment at 2:00 PM times out, the system marks the appointment cancelled but does not re-advertise the 2:00-2:30 and 2:30-3:00 windows back to the available-slots queue. This causes those windows to remain unavailable in the patron-facing UI despite staff member being idle. Gap discovered during scenario testing on October 18 during manual test run by QA lead Maria Chen. Reproduction steps: (1) book appointment for service, (2) reach appointment time in staging environment (time-travel via test harness), (3) wait 31 minutes, (4) query available slots for same service/staff/day, (5) slots do not appear. Tested across all three branches; gap reproduced 100% of test attempts (8 attempts total). Root cause: cancellation event handler at queue-management layer missing integration point. Fix implemented October 19: added eventEmitter.emit('slots_freed') call in cancellation handler, routing freed windows back through availability-compute microservice. No database migration required. Post-fix validation: 12 manual test runs all correct; slots reappear in patron UI within 3 seconds of timeout trigger. Automated regression test added to prevent recurrence. This gap would have caused significant pilot friction: orphaned staff time would compound daily, creating perception of unavailable capacity. Repair completed; release candidate now includes fix.

---

## ENTRY 5: 2026-11-01

Sprint 3 completed with cancellation workflow fully operational. All seven cancellation scenarios implemented and tested. Patron self-service cancellation allows booking revision up to 24 hours before appointment; cancellations within 24 hours flagged as late-notice and captured for operational review. Staff emergency cancellation (immediate) tested under simulated outage conditions: 15-minute cascade email sent to all affected patrons, automatic SMS to high-priority bookings (same-day or critical services). Rescheduling-as-cancellation path integrated; patron rebooking flow completed in single UI transaction. Administrative bulk cancellation (used for branch closures or staff leave) tested with 150-slot cancellations; processing time 2.1 seconds. Phone-bridge cancellation (staff fielding patron requests over phone) partially automated with manual confirmation step. Automatic timeout-based cancellations running in staging; tested across 430 timeout events, all handled correctly with zero missed notifications. Code coverage: 81%. Database schema now 54 tables. Total automated tests: 218. Performance baseline: availability query 285ms average (improved from 340ms in September), cancellation processing 1.2 seconds per event. Manual regression testing across all three branches (Central, Riverside, Hillcrest) conducted October 27-November 1 by combined QA and product team (35 test cases per branch). One minor UI bug found in cancellation confirmation modal (text truncation on longer service names); fixed and revalidated. System declared ready for internal pilot on November 1.

---

## ENTRY 6: 2026-11-03

Internal pilot launch approved by Captain Victoria Ramos on November 2. Pilot scope: live scheduling at Central Library for reference consultation and computer literacy training only (limiting initial demand footprint). Staff volunteers: 8 librarians across three shifts. Real patron bookings enabled November 3 starting 9:00 AM. First-day metrics: 47 appointments booked across two service types, 3 cancellations (all patron-initiated self-service, each within 24-hour window). Cancellation notifications delivered within 4 minutes of action; one SMS delivery delayed to 47 minutes (investigated, Clarity Messaging attributed to queue backlog, not our code). No system errors logged. Appointment confirmation emails sent and opened: 44 of 47 (93.6% open rate within 2 hours, higher than staging 64% - likely reflects real patron engagement). Staff reports good experience with availability display; librarians confirmed they could see opening windows clearly and no schedule conflicts occurred despite manual calendar integration. One staff member reported confusion about rescheduling workflow (product team to review UX), resolved with brief phone training. Notification delays being monitored closely; current 24-hour average: 98.1% SMS delivery within 5 minutes, 100% email delivery within 2 minutes. Database performing well under live load: query response times 312ms average (within bounds). Zero unplanned outages. Monitoring dashboards reporting nominal operation. Pilot satisfaction survey sent to early adopters; 6 responses received (small sample), all positive. Next milestone: extend pilot to document scanning service (45 min appointments) on November 5 pending Captain approval.

---

## ENTRY 7: 2026-11-04

System under live operation for 24 hours. Pilot expanded slightly today: document scanning service (45-minute appointments) added at 10:00 AM. Two additional staff members (scanning specialists) volunteered. Second-day metrics: 23 new appointments booked (total 70 active bookings), 2 cancellations (1 patron self-service, 1 staff-initiated emergency due to equipment failure). Emergency cancellation tested under unplanned stress: staff member cancelled a 2:00 PM scanning slot due to scanner malfunction. Cascade email triggered to three affected patrons within 61 seconds; all three were offered alternative time windows automatically. Two rebooked immediately via UI, one requested phone assistance (handled by reference desk staff). No technical failures during this event. Performance holding steady: 298ms average query time, database CPU utilization 34%. Automated alerts triggered twice during day: one false positive (database connection pool spike that self-resolved), one real alert (notification queue backing up briefly during high-volume confirmation period - 10:30-11:00 AM). Queue recovery to normal depth: 7 minutes. Root cause of queue spike: Clarity Messaging experienced transient slowdown (confirmed via their status page). Our retry logic absorbed the delay without data loss. Code review completed for database migration scripts targeting November 8 deployment window (new pilot metrics table for capture additional operational data). Migration scripts validated in staging environment replica. Vendor credential renewal for SMS service (Clarity) confirmed through November 2027; no interruption risk. Staff volunteers continuing to report positive experience.

---

## ENTRY 8: 2026-11-04 (EVENING)

Evidence limitation discovered during evening operations review. Pilot metrics collected since November 3 are statistically thin: 70 total appointments across 24 hours, drawn from only 10 patron-volunteers and 8 staff members. Cancellation data reflects exactly 2 patron-initiated and 2 staff-initiated events - insufficient for pattern analysis. Specifically, the cancellation-flow repair tested extensively in September-October relied on timeout scenarios (grace-period expiration), but the live pilot has yet to produce a real timeout-based cancellation under normal conditions. The October fix for the state-machine gap was validated against 12 manual test timeouts and 430 staging timeouts, but the specific sequence of events (timeout trigger, slot re-advertisement, patron re-booking the freed slot) has not been observed in production with real patron behavior. Automated monitoring shows the timeout handler firing (zero missed timeouts detected), but actual patron uptake of re-advertised slots has not yet been measured. Current operational window too narrow: we have bookings, cancellations, and notifications confirmed to work, but the end-to-end cancellation-recovery cycle (timeout -> free slots -> patron rebooking) remains untested under real-world conditions. Additional data collection will be required to fully validate the October repair. Estimated time to accumulate sufficient timeout-driven cancellation events: 7-10 days at current booking volume (requires approximately 8-12 no-show events). This limitation is documented in the November 8 Captain decision brief.

---

## ENTRY 9: 2026-11-05

Project Lantern 4 internal pilot now in day 3 of operation. Cumulative bookings: 117 appointments. Staff coverage expanded to include Riverside Branch starting this morning (adding 4 additional staff volunteers, 2 service types). Central Library and Riverside Branch both reporting smooth operations with no critical incidents. Third major cancellation scenario observed today: system-generated automatic cancellation due to staff unavailability (staff member called in sick at 7:30 AM, appointment window for 10:00 AM reference consultation affected). System detected unavailability through staff calendar integration, triggered automatic cancellation of single affected slot, cascade email delivered to patron within 73 seconds, patron rebooked immediately for afternoon window. This scenario validates a key workflow that had been tested extensively but never observed in live operation. Performance metrics holding strong: 94% of appointment confirmations opened within 2 hours, 99.2% SMS delivery within 5 minutes, 100% email delivery, zero unplanned outages. Database health nominal. Monitoring alerts trending down (yesterdays' false positives eliminated via tuning). One minor UX issue captured by staff: rescheduling confirmation modal closes too quickly on some devices, occasionally confusing staff about whether action completed; product team investigating (likely CSS animation timing, non-critical). Pilot satisfaction survey now showing 23 responses across staff and early-adopter patrons; average satisfaction 4.2/5.0, primary praise for ease of use and reliable notifications. Captain Ramos has scheduled November 8 decision briefing to determine trial expansion: proceed to full Hillcrest Commons launch (currently excluded, would add 100+ potential daily bookings) versus continue single-location controlled pilot through November 30.

---

## ENTRY 10: 2026-11-05 (DECISION BRIEFING SUMMARY)

Briefing prepared for Captain Ramos (scheduled November 8, 2:00 PM). Decision point: approve expansion of internal trial to full three-branch deployment with all five service types (reference consultation, computer literacy training, document scanning, children's story hour, and intake appointments), targeting November 8 launch, OR defer expansion to November 15 pending accumulation of additional production data under current controlled scope.

EXPANSION APPROVAL CASE: Three days of successful operation, 117 appointments processed error-free, all critical workflows validated (scheduling, notifications, patron/staff cancellation, emergency scenarios, automatic timeouts). Performance metrics and infrastructure handling current load without stress. Staff training burden minimal (7-minute onboarding sufficient). Technical readiness high. Pilot feedback positive. Estimated immediate benefit: 200+ daily bookings across full district, demonstrating district-wide viability within timeline for spring rollout decision.

DEFERRAL CASE: Cancellation-flow repair (October gap fix) not yet validated under full no-show timeout scenarios with real patron re-booking behavior. Current dataset insufficient: only 2 spontaneous no-show timeout cancellations observed, both too recent for patron reuse pattern analysis. Expansion would increase confidence risk (more staff, more bookings, more edge cases). Seven-day deferral allows accumulation of 8-12 timeout-driven cancellation events, sufficient for pattern validation. Minimal operational cost: pilot remains functional, staff volunteers willing to continue, patrons retain quality service. Risk of deferral: delays final rollout decision by one week, compresses November contingency buffer for any discovered issues.

RECOMMENDATION: Defer expansion to November 15 pending evidence accumulation. Core workflows validated; timeout-recovery evidence gap is narrow and resolvable within deferral window. Single gap represents material risk if expanded prematurely to high-volume deployment. If trial deferred, real-world timeout cancellation patterns will be observable by November 11, triggering full expansion confidence by November 15. If trial proceeds with expansion November 8 as scheduled, system will operate under conditions where the timeout-recovery repair has not been observed in production, carrying unknown operational risk and potential November rollout delay if issues emerge. Recommendation documents evidence limiter and proposes data-driven decision gate for November 8 morning (proceeding based on overnight timeout statistics).

---

End Report
